Approve adding the non-blocking lane.

title: Retry policy for calls from the service to the internal ledger API
question: Should the service adopt capped exponential backoff with jitter for its calls to the internal ledger API?
markdown:
## Summary

When the internal ledger API at `ledger.example.internal` is slow, the service retries at once and without limit. During the last slowdown this tripled the load on the ledger. This request proposes a bounded retry policy.

## Change

- Retry only on timeouts and on 502, 503 and 504 responses.
- Never retry on 4xx responses.
- Use exponential backoff: 200 ms, 400 ms, 800 ms, then stop.
- Add random jitter of up to 100 ms to each wait.
- Send the same idempotency key on every attempt, so a repeated write is safe.
- Count retries in the existing metrics as `ledger_retry_total`.

The policy lives in one wrapper function. All six call sites already go through that function, so no call site changes.

## Risk

Some requests will now fail after three attempts instead of hanging. Callers already handle this error, and the operator will see it in the metric.

## Rollback

Set `ledger.retry.enabled=false` in the service settings. This restores the old behaviour without a deploy.

## Decision needed

Approve the policy and the new metric.

title: Schema migration: add delivery_note column to the orders table
question: Should the order service run an additive migration that adds a nullable delivery_note column to its orders table?
markdown:
## Summary

The order service needs to store an optional delivery note that customers type at checkout. Today the note is dropped. This request adds one column to the orders table, which only the order service owns.

## Change

Migration `0042_add_delivery_note`:

```sql
ALTER TABLE orders ADD COLUMN delivery_note TEXT NULL;
```

- The column is nullable and has no default, so the change is fast and does not rewrite rows.
- No existing column is changed or removed.
- No other service reads this table.
- The code that writes the note ships in a later release, behind a flag.

The migration was run against a copy of staging data. It finished in under one second.

## Risk

Very low. Old code ignores the new column.

## Rollback

A down migration exists. It is only needed if the column must go before any notes are written. After that, we would leave the column in place.

## Decision needed

Approve running migration 0042 in staging and then in production during the normal deploy window.

title: Lint rule: forbid bare except clauses in the reporting service
question: Should the reporting service enable a lint rule that rejects bare except clauses in new and changed code?
markdown:
## Summary

The reporting service has many bare `except:` clauses. They hide real errors, including keyboard interrupts and typos in variable names. Two recent incidents took hours to find for this reason.

## Change

- Turn on the existing linter rule `E722` in the lint config of `<owner>/<repo>`.
- Apply it only to files changed in a pull request, using the linter's diff mode.
- Add a short page to the developer docs that explains the rule and shows the preferred form, `except SomeError:`.
- Add one line to the dashboard config so the count of remaining bare excepts appears on the existing code health dashboard.

Existing files are not rewritten by this request. They will be cleaned up as people touch them.

## Impact

Developers may need a few extra minutes when they edit an old file. The rule can be skipped on a single line with a comment and a reason.

## Rollback

Remove `E722` from the lint config.

## Decision needed

Approve enabling the rule in diff mode.

title: Bounded retry policy for the export worker
question: Should the export worker adopt a bounded retry policy of at most four attempts with exponential backoff on timeouts and 503 responses?
markdown:
## Summary

The export worker in the service calls the report store once per job. When the store returns a timeout, the job fails. The operator must then restart it by hand. This request adds a bounded retry policy so that short timeouts recover on their own.

## Change

- Retry on timeouts and on HTTP 503 only. Do not retry on 4xx responses.
- Use at most 4 attempts in total.
- Wait 500 ms before the first retry, then double the wait each time, up to a cap of 8 seconds.
- Add random jitter of up to 20 percent to each wait.
- Log each retry at info level with the job id and the attempt number.
- Emit a counter named `export_retry_total`.

The policy lives in one new file, `retry.go`, and is wired in at the single call site. No other callers change.

## Testing

Unit tests cover each retryable and non-retryable status. A fake clock checks the wait times. The change ships behind the existing `export_v2` flag, which is already on in staging.

## Rollback

Revert the commit. No data or config changes are involved.

title: Lint rule to flag bare print calls in library code
question: Should the shared lint config add a `no-bare-print` rule at warning level for files under `src/`?
markdown:
## Summary

Several modules in `<owner>/<repo>` still write debug output with bare `print` calls. These lines bypass the structured logger, so their output never reaches the log pipeline. This request adds a lint rule that flags new `print` calls in library code.

## Change

Add the rule `no-bare-print` to the shared lint config in `lint/rules.yaml`. The rule:

- applies to files under `src/`;
- skips files under `scripts/` and `tests/`, where printing is normal;
- reports a short hint to use `log.debug` instead.

The rule is set to `warn` for the first two weeks. After that, a follow-up request will ask to raise it to `error`. Existing calls are listed in a baseline file so that the check passes today. The baseline holds 37 entries.

## Impact

No runtime behavior changes. CI time rises by less than one second on a full run. Developers who add a new `print` in `src/` will see a warning in their editor and in the CI summary.

## Testing

The rule has fixture tests for a flagged file, a skipped test file and an inline suppression comment.

title: Add a nullable channel column to the orders table
question: Should the order service apply migration `0042_add_order_channel`, which adds one nullable column and one concurrent index to its own orders table?
markdown:
## Summary

The order service needs to record which channel placed each order. Today the channel is guessed from logs. This request adds one nullable column to the service's own database. No other service reads this table.

## Change

Migration `0042_add_order_channel` runs:

```sql
ALTER TABLE orders ADD COLUMN channel TEXT NULL;
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY orders_channel_idx ON orders (channel);
```

The column has no default, so the change does not rewrite the table. The index is built concurrently, so writes are not blocked. The code writes the field for new orders only. Old rows stay null, and the read path treats null as `unknown`.

## Rollout

1. Apply the migration in staging and run the order test suite.
2. Apply it in production during normal hours. The table holds about 2 million rows. The index build should take under five minutes.
3. Deploy the code that writes the field.

## Risk

Low. The migration is additive. If the index build fails, it can be retried. The column is still usable without the index.

title: Queue health dashboard for the notification service
question: Should the team add a four-panel queue health dashboard for the notification service, built only from existing metrics?
markdown:
## Summary

The operator has no single view of queue health for the notification service. This request adds one dashboard built from metrics that the service already emits.

## Change

Create a dashboard named `notifications / queue` in the team folder of the metrics tool at `metrics.example.internal`. It has four panels:

1. Queue depth, per queue, over the last 6 hours.
2. Age of the oldest message, with a line at the 5 minute target.
3. Messages processed per minute.
4. Worker error rate, as a percentage of processed messages.

The dashboard is read-only for viewers and editable by the team. It uses the existing data source. No new metrics, exporters or alerts are added. The JSON definition is checked into `dashboards/notifications-queue.json`, so it can be reviewed and restored from source.

## Notes

Panel 2 will later back an alert. That alert is out of scope here and will come in its own request. The time range defaults to 6 hours, and any viewer can change it for their own session. The dashboard needs no new permissions.

title: Enable the CI build cache for dependencies
question: Should CI for `<owner>/<repo>` enable the built-in build cache for the `target/deps` directory with a seven-day expiry, while release builds stay uncached?
markdown:
## Summary

CI builds for `<owner>/<repo>` recompile every dependency on each run. A full build takes about 14 minutes. This request turns on the build cache that the CI system already offers to every project.

## Change

- In `.ci/build.yaml`, set `cache.enabled: true`.
- Use the cache key `deps-{{ lockfile hash }}-{{ toolchain version }}`.
- Cache only the `target/deps` directory. Do not cache test output or release artifacts.
- Set cache entries to expire after 7 days.

The cache uses the project storage that CI already provides. No new secrets or settings are needed. Release builds keep `cache.enabled: false`, so shipped binaries are always built clean.

## Expected result

On a trial branch, warm builds took 5 minutes. Cold builds after a lockfile change took the same 14 minutes as today.

## Risk

A stale cache could hide a build problem. The key includes the lockfile hash and the toolchain version to prevent this. Any developer can skip the cache for one run by adding `[no-cache]` to the commit message.

title: Add a bounded retry policy for usage record posts
question: Should the service adopt a three-attempt retry policy with jittered backoff for posting usage records, behind a config flag?
markdown:
## Summary

The service posts usage records to the billing queue at example.internal. Today a single failed call sends the record straight to the error log. We want a small retry policy so that short network blips do not lose records.

## Change

- Retry failed calls up to three times.
- Wait 200 ms, then 400 ms, then 800 ms. Add up to 50 ms of random jitter to each wait.
- Retry only on timeouts and 503 responses. Do not retry on any 4xx response.
- After the last attempt, write the record to the existing local dead-letter file, as we do today.
- Add one counter for retries and one counter for final failures.

The extra wait is under two seconds per record. Posting already runs on a background worker, so no user request gets slower.

## Testing

Unit tests cover each status code. A test against a fake server checks the backoff timing within a small tolerance.

## Rollback

The policy sits behind a config flag, `usage_retry_enabled`. Setting it to false restores the old behavior without a deploy.

title: Lint rule: disallow bare except clauses
question: Should we enable a lint rule in <owner>/<repo> that fails the build on bare except clauses in new or changed files?
markdown:
## Summary

Bare `except:` clauses catch everything, including keyboard interrupts and system exit. They have hidden real bugs in the past. We want the linter to flag them.

## Change

Turn on the existing bare-except check in the lint config of <owner>/<repo>. The check runs only on files that a pull request adds or changes. Old files are not touched, so no one has to fix the whole codebase at once.

A developer who really needs a broad catch can write `except Exception:` instead. If a bare catch is truly required, a one-line ignore comment with a reason is allowed.

The change is four lines in the lint config and one paragraph in the contributing guide.

## Impact

We ran the check over the last month of merged pull requests. It would have flagged six of them. All six were easy to fix.

## Rollback

Remove the four config lines.

title: Add a nullable last_seen_at column to the sessions table
question: Should the session service run a migration that adds a nullable last_seen_at column and a concurrent index to its sessions table?
markdown:
## Summary

The session service cannot tell how long a session has been idle. Support asks for this often. We want to record the last time each session was used.

## Change

One migration in the session service's own database:

- Add a column `last_seen_at`, type timestamp with time zone, nullable, no default.
- Build an index on `last_seen_at` with the concurrent option, so writes are not blocked.

The service code will set `last_seen_at` on each authenticated request, at most once per minute per session, to keep write load low.

There is no backfill. Existing rows keep a null value until the session is next used. Readers treat null as "unknown".

No other service reads this table. No existing column changes. No data is removed.

## Testing

The migration ran on a copy of the staging database. It finished in under a minute. The index build took most of that time.

## Rollback

The down migration drops the new index and the new column. The new column holds only data written after this change, so dropping it loses nothing the service used before.

title: Enable a shared build cache for CI compile steps
question: Should CI for <owner>/<repo> use the existing internal artifact store as a build cache for compile steps?
markdown:
## Summary

CI builds in <owner>/<repo> take about eighteen minutes. Most of that time goes to compiling modules that did not change. A build cache would let jobs reuse earlier outputs.

## Change

- Point the build tool's remote cache at the internal artifact store we already run at cache.example.internal.
- CI jobs on the main branch may read from and write to the cache.
- CI jobs on pull requests may only read. This stops an unmerged branch from filling the cache with bad outputs.
- Cache entries expire after fourteen days.
- The cache key includes the compiler version and the lockfile hash.

The CI runners already reach the artifact store, so no new network rules or accounts are needed.

## Expected effect

In a trial on a fork, warm builds dropped to about seven minutes. Cold builds were unchanged.

## Rollback

Remove the cache settings from the CI config. Builds then compile from scratch, as they do today.

title: Lower health check logs to debug and add request ids to access logs
question: Should the gateway service log health check requests at debug level and add a request id field to every access log line?
markdown:
## Summary

The gateway service writes one info line for every health check. Health checks arrive every two seconds from each load balancer. These lines make up close to forty percent of the gateway's log volume and bury the lines people need.

We also cannot easily follow one request across the gateway and the services behind it.

## Change

- Log requests to `/healthz` and `/readyz` at debug level instead of info. Failed health checks stay at warning level.
- Add a `request_id` field to every access log line. Use the incoming `X-Request-Id` header if it is present. Otherwise generate a new id and pass it on to the upstream service.

The log format stays JSON. Existing fields keep their names and order. The new field is added at the end.

## Testing

Unit tests check the level for each path and check that the id is reused when present.

## Rollback

Revert the commit. No stored data depends on this change.
